To proceed, I’ll guide you through a few checks and steps on your device to diagnose and resolve the MMS issue. Are you able to follow instructions on your phone right now? If so, please let me know, and I’ll provide the first step.
Yes, I have my phone with me and can follow your instructions. Please let me know what you’d like me to do first.

Great! Let’s start by checking your phone’s status bar to see if there are any obvious issues with your network connection or mobile data.

Please check your status bar and let me know if you see any of the following:
- Airplane mode icon (✈️)
- No signal or very low signal bars
- “4G”, “5G”, or similar network type indicator
- Mobile data icon (📱 or similar)
- Wi-Fi icon (📡)

Alternatively, if your phone allows, you can use any diagnostic tool or setting that shows your current network status and icons. Please describe what you see, especially regarding signal strength, network type, and whether mobile data is enabled.
Status Bar: ✈️ Airplane Mode | 🔋 80%
My status bar is showing the Airplane Mode icon (✈️), and the battery is at 80%. I don’t see any signal bars or network type indicators at the moment. What should I do next?

Airplane Mode disables all wireless connections, including cellular service and mobile data, which are required for sending MMS messages. 

Please turn off Airplane Mode on your phone. Once you have done that, check if your signal bars and network type (such as “4G” or “5G”) appear in the status bar. Let me know what you see after turning off Airplane Mode.

1. Please enable mobile data on your phone.
2. After enabling mobile data, check if you can switch your network mode to a higher speed (preferably “4G” or “5G” if available). This is usually found in your phone’s network or cellular settings under “Preferred network type” or similar.
